## PLAN ROUND 1 · publish · task first-edition

**Facts found**
- Three of the five runbooks name an internal host or a secret path, one line each:
  - `runbooks/disk-full.md:3`: host `db-primary-01.int.example.net`
  - `runbooks/queue-backlog.md:3`: host `jobs-01.int.example.net`
  - `runbooks/cert-expiry.md:3`: secret path `secret/platform/acme-token`
  - `deploy-rollback.md` and `dns-failure.md` name neither (search for `int.example.net`, `secret/`).
- `scripts/check.sh` enforces two rules: every runbook opens with `Use when`, and every `./` link
  resolves. A grep for hosts and secret paths would fit the same loop.
- `STANDARDS.md` has one rule: a runbook's first line says when to use it. It says nothing about
  hosts, secrets, or comments.
- The repository has no publishing tooling: no `mkdocs.yml`, pandoc config, build script, or CI.
- Every format sits behind single sign-on, and one access group grants all three. So the audience
  is that group's membership, whatever the format (`context/publishing.md`).
- `runbooks/dns-failure.md` covers the case where "internal names stop resolving".

**Currency**
- cwd: no currency command

**Questions**

1. **First edition's format: one PDF on the internal file share, a static MkDocs site on the
   internal docs host, or a Markdown index page in this repository?**
   - **rec:** one PDF. Only a PDF someone has downloaded still opens when internal names stop
     resolving, which is the failure the DNS runbook covers. pandoc, the standard converter,
     builds it, so we write no converter. A site needs a build and a host, and the project has
     no CI. An index page needs repository access, which misses the goal's "without cloning".
     The cost: every edit means a new PDF, and old copies linger.
   - **changes:** the task adds a pandoc build of the five runbooks into one PDF, to be published
     on the internal file share. No site config and no hosting.
2. **First edition's audience: on-call engineers only, or on-call engineers plus the support team,
   who asked for read access at the last quarterly review?**
   - **rec:** both. The redaction is small: two internal hostnames and one secret path, in three
     runbooks. Leaving support out now means another edition later.
   - **changes:** if support is included, the task first redacts those three lines and adds a
     rule that keeps hosts and secret paths out of new runbooks. Once published to support, that
     can't be undone. If on-call only, neither happens and the runbooks stay as written.

**reply:** "1 ok, 2 ok", or your answer to each

Round 2 depends on these answers. If support is included, it asks how to redact (remove, use
placeholders, or move to an on-call-only page) and whether the clean-runbooks rule goes in the
check or in `STANDARDS.md`. Depending on the format, it also asks how readers can tell which copy
is current, and who uploads the edition. No agent can reach the file share or the docs host, so
that upload will probably be your step.

One thing outside this task: `scripts/check.sh` only checks links that start with `./`. A Markdown
index could add links it wouldn't check. I'll treat this as a note unless you want it in scope.
